newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's Sat1 hails commercial-free TV a success.
newsitem.headline: Germany's Sat1 hails commercial-free TV a success.

text.p: German television station Sat1 said on Monday it had beaten its competition on Saturday night with a new marketing strategy for commercial television -- an evening of programming without advertising.

Sat1 said it had posted spectacular ratings, particularly among the key demographic group of 14 to 49 year olds, by trading ad interruptions for an evening of top Hollywood films sponsored by Kulmbacher Reichel Braeu AG beer brewers.

"We won more from this type of presentation than we ever could have got with commercial interruptions," said Sat1 spokeswoman Kristina Fassler of the evening, which included brief announcements that Kulmbacher was the sponsor.

The network pulled in a 19.2 percent market share among viewers above the age of three, about five points above nearest competitor ARD, and 22.4 percent of 14 to 49 year-old viewers, seven points ahead of rival private broadcaster RTL.
Fassler dismissed industry criticism that the Sat1 strategy would undermine German television advertising.
"It is ridiculous to say that advertising-free programming would turn viewers off commercials just when they have got used to them," she said.

Fassler declined to say if the network planned other sponsored film evenings for the future, aside from a further three scheduled with Kulmbacher. The station also did not release financial details about the Kulmbacher deal.
The network showed hit U.S. films "Dances with Wolves", "Internal Affairs" and "Dangerous Liaisons".

While some private stations have showed individual films without commercials, such as Steven Spielberg's "Schindler's List" on ProSieben, Sat1 said its evening of commercial-free films was an innovative marketing approach.
The film evening concept was developed with Hamburg advertising agency, Springer & Jacoby, Bloecher & Partner SponsorConsult and Mediahaus Stroebel, Fassler said.
